subject: Post-call: FintechAI - cost/pricing follow-up & latency vs cost options
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron@fintechai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — cost/pricing and latency trade-offs

Aaron — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Use case: customer support assistant + automated summarization for transactions (primarily text completions and some embeddings for retrieval).
- Current pilot target: ~20M tokens/month to start, expected to grow to ~100M tokens/month over 12 months if latency and quality meet expectations.
- Latency SLO: aiming for p95 <= 250ms for short chat completions; some background batching for lower-priority summarization is acceptable.
- Budget signals: target unit economics around $250–$350 per 1M tokens for the initial pilot; open to higher for guaranteed SLO.

Key open questions for pricing qualification (please confirm):
1) Typical prompt+response size (tokens): you estimated ~600 tokens per interaction on average?
2) Traffic shape: steady 24/7 or peak windows (we heard morning/evening peaks)?
3) Any compliance constraints (PII/HIPAA) that would push you to Private deployment?

Where we can help (options to balance latency vs cost):
- Hosted Standard (lowest friction): streaming responses, per-token pricing. Good for fast time-to-value but variable unit costs at peak.
- Dedicated Reserved (predictable unit economics): reserved capacity with committed throughput. Lower $/1M with a monthly commit; tuning batch sizes can further lower cost but will increase tail latency for some requests unless we use streaming for chat routes.
- Private/VPC (for regulated data): enterprise pricing; comparable unit economics to Dedicated with additional infra fees.

Tuning levers I recommend we discuss on the follow-up tech call:
- Streaming vs batching: stream chat routes to meet p95 SLOs; batch summarization pipelines to improve throughput and lower $/1M.
- Batch window and max tokens per batch: we can recommend conservative defaults (50–100ms batching window) that reduce cost with minimal p95 impact.
- Model tiering: route sensitive low-latency interactions to smaller context, optimized models; route high-quality/offline tasks to larger/quantized models.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the three items above (average tokens per interaction, traffic shape, compliance)?
- I attached a quick usage worksheet (FintechAI_estimated_usage.xlsx) with the assumptions I used for the $/1M target — please review.
- If that looks right, I’ll loop in Rishi (pricing) and Neha (solutions) and we can do a 30-min technical + pricing sync early next week to propose a 3-tier pricing plan for the pilot.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-2187

Attachments: FintechAI_estimated_usage.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aaron Lee <aaron@fintechai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — cost/pricing and latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the call. Quick answers inline: 

1) Average tokens: we roughly estimated 600 tokens per interaction (prompt+response), though responses can spike to ~1.2k for complex threads.
2) Traffic shape: steady baseline with two peaks (UTC 14:00–16:00 and 22:00–23:30); baseline is about 0.7x of peak.
3) Compliance: not HIPAA right now, but PII-sensitive data handling is required — likely hosted Dedicated will be fine; Private for now is optional.

Budget: target $/1M tokens closer to $300 for the pilot; we can stretch to $400 if you can guarantee p95 <= 250ms on chat routes.

Two clarifying questions: 
- For streaming + batching hybrid, can we have per-route config so chat is streamed and summarization uses batching?
- What batch window would you recommend that balances cost vs p95 for short responses?

If you/your team can propose a few concrete price points (hosted standard / dedicated reserved / private) and the expected $/1M under our 20M and 100M token scenarios, that’ll help us get internal approval.

Appreciate it — Aaron
Aaron Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechAI
aaron@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron@fintechai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — cost/pricing and latency trade-offs

Aaron — great, thanks for the clarifications. Short answers: yes, per-route config is standard — you can stream chat routes and enable batching for summarization/embeddings pipelines.

Recommended batching guidance (initial conservative defaults):
- Chat routes (low-latency): streaming enabled; batching disabled or extremely short window (<= 20ms) to keep p95 tight.
- Summarization/async tasks: 50–200ms batching window depending on throughput; 100ms tends to be a good middle ground and yields significant cost savings on token-heavy jobs.

Proposed pricing sketch (ballpark, provisional — Rishi will finalize):
- Hosted Standard: $450 / 1M tokens (pay-as-you-go). Low setup, higher variance at peaks.
- Dedicated Reserved (monthly commit): $300 / 1M tokens at 20M commit; $250 / 1M tokens at 100M commit. Includes predictable throughput and priority queuing to improve p95.
- Private/VPC: $350 / 1M tokens + infra fee (generally comparable to Dedicated after infra amortization).

Notes on SLOs:
- Dedicated with priority routing + streaming for chat should hit p95 <= 250ms for the short 600-token flows in most regions. 99th percentile latency may require higher headroom or a higher-tier instance.
- Batching lowers average cost but can hurt tail latency; we’ll recommend streaming for any route where p95 matters.

I’m attaching a quick PDF summary of the tiers (Redwood_pricing_tiers_v2.pdf) and the worksheet I mentioned. If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-min sync with Rishi (pricing) and your infra lead for Monday. 

Would Monday 10:00 AM PT work for you?

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_pricing_tiers_v2.pdf (summary)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron@fintechai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — cost/pricing and latency trade-offs

Looping in quick pricing detail and a suggested pilot MAP structure. 

Marissa captured the right levers. Additional specifics from pricing side: 
- Pilot (20M tokens/month): propose Dedicated Reserved at $300 / 1M with a 3-month minimum commit. This gives predictable billing and priority capacity which materially helps p95 latency.
- Growth tier (100M tokens/month): $250 / 1M with a quarterly review and auto-scaling buffer; we can include a 5% buffer to handle peak windows.
- Hosted Standard remains available for proof-of-concept but we recommend Dedicated for production pilot given your p95 requirement.

Operational notes: 
- Per-route configuration: yes — we’ll include route definitions in the MAP and a default streaming policy for chat.
- Batching window: we typically recommend starting at 100ms for summarization pipelines and tune down if p95 impact is too high. We can provide A/B tests on batching windows during the pilot.

Next steps from our side:
1) I’ll put together a one-page MAP with the three options and estimated monthly invoice examples under 20M and 100M token profiles.
2) If FintechAI signs the 3-month pilot, we’ll lock the $300 / 1M pricing for that period and schedule an architecture review with Neha.

Marissa — I’ve added a placeholder HubSpot deal and a shared Drive folder (link below). I’ll have the MAP draft by end of day Friday.

Thanks,
